summary: NHTSA summarized and analyzed all comments, and in response to concerns about sulfate emissions (raised by commenters including FEA), dropped the discussion of sulfate emissions from the final EIS and revised the discussion of noble metal use to reflect a smaller increase in platinum and palladium usage.
text:
All comments have been summarized and analyzed in a previous section. The more substantive comments related to the effect of the MY 1979 emission standard for NPA's, the potential for reducing the weight of NPA's by MY 1979, the effect on NPA fuel economy of the MY 1979 emission standard for California, the increase in sulfate emissions in MY 1979 due to catalytic converter size increases, and the increased use of noble metals in catalysts for MY 1979. As a result of the analysis of all comments the agency is making several changes to the draft EIS. Gasoline savings are described in this final EIS relative to a range of fuel economies. The range was established by applying the maximum and minimum possible fuel economy penalties of the MY 1979 emission standard to the originally proposed AFES. Also, gasoline savings are shown for two classes of NPA's. The two classes are 1) recreational type NPA's with off-road capability and 2) all other NPA's.

The effects of the MY 1979 emission standard for California, according to the information applied by the domestic manufacturers, are incorporated. The manufacturers' comments on the impossibility of weight reduction are not incorporated because the application of weight reduction is only to GM and they did not say it was impossible. The discussion of sulfate emissions has been dropped and the discussion of noble metal use has been revised to indicate a smaller increase in the use of platinum and palladium.
